concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
question: Which of the following acts reduced the number of directors of East India Company?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Charter Act of 1853**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Charter Act of 1853** was the last of the Charter Acts passed by the British Parliament for the East India Company.
 
• This Act reduced the number of directors of the East India Company from **24 to 18**, with six directors to be nominated by the British Crown.
 
• It marked the beginning of the separation of legislative and executive functions of the Governor-General's Council by introducing a separate Legislative Council.
 
• The Act did not specify a fixed period for the continuation of the East India Company, unlike previous Charter Acts.
 
• It was a significant step towards the development of a parliamentary system in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Charter Act of 1833:** This Act centralized the administration in India by making the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India and abolished the monopoly of the East India Company in trade.
 
• **Charter Act of 1813:** Ended the commercial monopoly of the East India Company except for trade in tea and trade with China and allowed Christian missionaries to propagate their religion in India.
 
• **Charter Act of 1793:** Renewed the company's charter for another 20 years and allowed it to retain its monopoly on trade in India.
 
• **Governor-General's Council:** The Charter Act of 1853 expanded the Governor-General's Council to include six new legislative members, paving the way for greater legislative deliberation.
 
• **Impact:** The Act is considered a precursor to the Indian Councils Act of 1861, which further reformed the legislative structure in British India.
